newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HEINEKEN SEES FURTHER U.S. EXPORT GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: HEINEKEN SEES FURTHER U.S. EXPORT GROWTH.

text.p: Heineken NV, Europe's biggest brewer, sees good business opportunities in the still growing import segment of the U.S. beer market, board member Guus Lubsen told the American chamber of commerce on Tuesday.

Dividing the U.S. beer market into four segments -- savings, lights, standard and sophisticated -- Lubsen said annual growth in the sophisticated segment had accelerated to 14 percent over the last five years from seven percent in the last 10.
"There is a current explosion away from standard beer in the direction of sophisticated beer. There's roughly a 10 percent growth over the last five years in imports," he said.
Lubsen sub-divided the sophisticated segment into import beer, super premium beer, national specialty beer, regional specialty beer and microbreweries & brewpubs.
He said the growing interest in microbreweries and brewpubs did not worry him, adding consumers were likely to be tempted to try a Heineken once they had turned away from standard beers.
He said the U.S. beer market was the only market in the world with a large and growing light (low-calorie) beer market.
In addition to its flagship Heineken brand, the Dutch company already sells Amstel Light in the U.S. and will soon launch the regular Amstel and Amstel 1870 brands in the U.S.
Heineken estimates it has two to 2.5 percent of the total U.S. beer market and 5.6 percent of the world market, making it the world's second biggest brewer after Anheuser-Busch .
Lubsen said China, if it maintains its current rate of growth, would overtake the U.S. beer market by the year 2001.

Total Chinese beer consumption was currently expanding each year by an amount equivalent to the entire consumption of France, he said, but annual per capita consumption was still only a relatively modest 16 litres.
By comparison, annual per capita consumption in the Netherlands was 85 to 90 litres, he said.
